previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A 58-year-old male with a history of acute myeloid leukemia in remission following allogeneic stem cell transplant and chronic graft-versus-host disease was admitted for worsening shortness of breath. Imaging revealed right upper lobe consolidation consistent with pneumonia, prompting initiation of broad-spectrum antibiotics. A bronchoscopy with biopsy was performed, which led to a postprocedural pneumothorax requiring chest tube placement. The infectious workup was negative, but clinical improvement was observed with antibiotic therapy. An echocardiogram showed reduced ejection fraction, leading to initiation of metoprolol. GVHD management included dose adjustments to ruxolitinib and sirolimus. The patient stabilized, completed treatment, and was discharged home with follow-up arranged in oncology, cardiology, and pulmonary clinics.
